name: contribution_messages
description: The dialogue on one contribution: what the member wrote, what the moderator answered, and the moderator-only notes beside it.

columns.name: user_id
columns.description: Who wrote it — member or moderator. is_moderator says which.

columns.name: is_moderator
columns.description: Whether the author acted as a moderator when writing this. Not the same as the author holding the moderator role today — a role can be taken away, the message stays what it was.

indexes.name: contribution_messages_contribution_id_idx
indexes.note: Legacy declares it with a bare @Index() on the column, so TypeORM names it. Migration 0075 added it; the generated name in a legacy database is not this one.

notes: MODERATOR messages are visible to moderators only. That is an access rule, not a display preference: a query serving a member must filter the type, not the frontend. See types/ContributionMessageType.json.
HISTORY rows are written by the system when a contribution changes, not by a person. user_id then holds whoever caused the change.

Legacy declares created_at and updated_at as datetime WITHOUT precision(3) — second precision. Two messages written in the same second do not order by timestamp; order by id. See types/Timestamp.json.
The entity carries both @CreateDateColumn/@UpdateDateColumn and a plain @Column for the same field. TypeORM takes the last one; the effective column is what is written here.
